title: Custom action on double click on "empty" desktop area
line: You can now assign a mouse action to a double-click on the empty desktop, for example opening the Application Launcher menu.
explanation: Mouse actions are stored by trigger string, and ContainmentActions::eventToString() turned a double-click into the same "LeftButton" trigger as a plain press, so a double-click could never have its own action. On top of that, Folder View swallows clicks on empty space (for rubber-band selection) and only replays a single press to the desktop, and the Mouse Actions page recorded every click as a single click. The change adds a separate "doubleclick:<button>" trigger that ContainmentItem handles (keeping the press when only a double-click action exists), makes Folder View replay double-clicks too, and lets the Mouse Actions page record and show them as "Left-Button Double-Click".

commits.message:
containmentitem: support mouse actions on double-click

ContainmentActions::eventToString() gave a double-click the same trigger
as a press, so no action could be assigned to it. Give it a separate
"doubleclick:" trigger and run its action from ContainmentItem.

BUG: 409616

shell: let the mouse actions model make double-click triggers

The mouse actions page could only turn single clicks and wheel events
into triggers. Add a method that returns the trigger of a double-click,
so that the page can record actions for double-clicks too.

BUG: 409616

desktop: support mouse actions on double-click

Folder View takes clicks on empty space and replays them to the desktop
as a press, so a double-click never reached the mouse actions. Replay it
too, and let the mouse actions page record and show double-clicks.

BUG: 409616

media.caption: Before: the Mouse Actions page can only record a click as Left-Button, a plain single click
After: double-clicking the recorder adds a Left-Button Double-Click action, here set to Application Launcher
Before: with the only possible Left-Button action, a single click on the empty desktop already opens the menu
After: a single click does nothing, a double-click opens the Application Launcher menu; rubber-band drag and right-click still work
